reference_action: Dense wet soil and poor drainage, with low light also identified. OP explicitly credited repotting into a well-draining planter with better soil and reported two new leaves. Improved soil/pot drainage is the confirmed central action; light was recommended but not explicitly confirmed in the outcome.

sources.reason: Video has no accessible substantive transcript; description promises tips without providing them.
Description reports a rescue but does not explain the actual steps, and transcript is unavailable.
Explicit repot from water-retentive peat into draining aroid mix, with pot-size/material and light improvements, matches the confirmed drainage intervention.

Cut rotten stems and reroot in water before eventual garden planting; a different rescue from repotting the existing plant in improved draining medium. Light overlap alone is not the explicitly confirmed action.
Explicit repot in really well-draining soil matches the confirmed intervention; pest products and propagation are extra alternatives.

actions.action: Water lightly after repotting and reduce watering
Use a smaller pot as alternative
Move closer to window for more light
Check moisture using fingers drainage holes and pot weight

resolved.reason: Overwatering from dense medium, relative pot size and low light is accurately explained, with the same drainage-improving repotting remedy and root checks before pruning.

harmfulness.reason: Root pruning follows examination and uses “sterile pruning shears.” The source retains partly functional foliage and checks moisture before watering, though repeated root disturbance from optional pot changes would be unnecessary.

specificity_accuracy.reason: The contrast between peat and a “much better draining potting mix” closely matches the confirmed soil/drainage problem. Smaller-pot and brighter-window options also address slow drying, though the source assumes some root rot not directly confirmed for the target.

feasibility.reason: The rescue sequence is clear and materials are named. Multiple repotting alternatives and the unspecified “good temperatures” target make the complete answer more involved than the short plan the OP followed.
